subject: Workarounds for legends that "fall" on top of each other

messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: Workarounds for legends that "fall" on top of each other
parts:
Hi,

When I do this using ggvis 0.1.0.99:
ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) + 
  layer_point()
the legends print on top of each other. The vignette for axes-legends alludes to this issue, and I can use this:

ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) + 
  layer_point() + 
  guide_legend("size", orient = "left")
as a workaround.

I know that this issue will get sorted out in the fullness of time, allowing the legends to find their own place, by themselves.

My question is this: is there something I can do now to specify manually the vertical position of a legend on the right side of the plot?

If this is not an easy thing, or if the best thing is to wait for the comprehensive solution, it is not the end of the world.

Thanks as always,

Ian

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Workarounds for legends that "fall" on top of each other
parts:
Hi Ian -

It looks like there's a bug in creating the legend section of the spec. This _should_ work, but doesn't:

ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) + 
  layer_point() +

guide_legend("size", properties = list(legend = props(y := 150)))

The problem is that in the spec, there should be a section that looks like this:
"legends" : [
  {
    "size" : "size",
    "orient" : "right",
    "properties" : {
      "legend" : {
        "y" : {
          "value" : 100
        }
      }
    },
    "title" : "hp"
  },
 ...
]

But instead the "properties" subsection looks like this, with an extra "update" in there:
  "properties" : {
    "legend" : {
      "update" : {
        "y" : {
          "value" : 150
        }
      }
    }
  }

Until it's fixed, if you're bold enough to edit the HTML output directly, you can remove the "update" layer in the JSON object.

Also, if you're looking at the plots in RStudio and find that it always points to a localhost address instead of directly to a file, you can use this to see the URL:
p <- ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) + 
  layer_point() + 
  guide_legend("size", properties = list(legend = props(y := 150)))
file <- print(p, launch = FALSE)
browseURL(file)

-Winston
